newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bund futures holding gains, further ranges seen.
newsitem.headline: Bund futures holding gains, further ranges seen.

text.p: Bund futures held early gains in exceptionally light trade on Monday with dealers aiming to keep the German market closely linked to Treasury prices which were stable ahead of a U.S. holiday.
Analysts said they expect Bunds to trade between psychological support at 100.00 and the contract high of 100.58 at least through Wednesday when the Federal Open Market Committee meets.
The December DTB Bund futures contract was up 17 basis points late in the day at 100.37 after trading in a narrow range of 100.20 and 100.42.
Analysts said if left alone, Bunds could edge toward 101.00, but that as usual, the Treasury market would dictate the direction of German debt.
Bunds have tracked Treasuries step-for-step since their rally last week, but some analysts expect Bunds to underperform if U.S. debt finds further reason to climb.
"If Treasuries rally, Bunds are sure to underperform even further," said Stuart Trow, fixed-income analyst at Norinchukin International Plc.
Since the start of October, the T-note/Bund spread has narrowed to 45 basis points from 71 basis points.

Analysts said they see further Treasury market outperformance because domestic German investors are almost absent from their own market while at least some domestic investors are buying Treasury bonds.

Although German economic indicators last week pointed at a slow economy, traders are still convinced that growth will pick up and that the German yield curve will resume flattening after some hints of steepening last week.
